title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps for K Consecutive Ones
summary: Given an array of integers consisting solely of 0s and 1s, and an integer k, determine the least number of adjacent swaps needed to ensure there are exactly k consecutive 1s in the array.
statement: Given an array of integers consisting solely of 0s and 1s, and an integer k, determine the least number of adjacent swaps needed to ensure there are exactly k consecutive 1s in the array.
constraints: nums has up to 100000 binary values and contains at least k ones.
One move swaps adjacent values; make some k ones occupy consecutive positions.
Return the minimum number of swaps.
reference_solution:
def minimum_swaps_for_consecutive_ones(nums,k):
    positions=[index-order for order,index in enumerate(i for i,value in enumerate(nums) if value)]
    prefix=[0]
    for value in positions:prefix.append(prefix[-1]+value)
    answer=float('inf')
    for left in range(len(positions)-k+1):
        right=left+k;middle=left+k//2;median=positions[middle]
        cost=median*(middle-left)-(prefix[middle]-prefix[left])
        cost+=(prefix[right]-prefix[middle+1])-median*(right-middle-1)
        answer=min(answer,cost)
    return answer

Subtract each one’s rank so consecutive target positions collapse to one common adjusted coordinate.
Use prefix sums to measure absolute distance to the median for every length-k adjusted-position window.
The median minimizes total absolute distance, and every optimal solution uses some consecutive group in the ordered list of original one positions.
